To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the energy utilization of a three-roll mill for grinding sor­ghum, wheat or corn is a function of the fast roll speed, the differential speed, and the roll gap setting.
the energy consumption of a three- roller mill for grain size reduction depends on the particle size of the material and the size reduction of the material.
the net specific energy and energy utilization both decreased as the roller gap was decreased, and as the roller speed was increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a three- roller mill for grinding sor ghum, wheat, or corn.
developing an understanding of how the energy consumption in a three- roller mill is affected by the operating parameters of the mill and by the physical properties of the grains.
developing a mathematical model that relates energy consumption and size reduction for a three-roll mill.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a three-roller milling system can be operated at lower energy consumption with a reduction in particle size of the milled product.
energy utilization is a function of the particle size distribution of the material, the particle size distribution and surface area of the product, and the mill variables.
the energy utilization of the three-roller mill is dependent on particle size, mill variables, and type of grain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NSEC and EU of a three- roller mill are influenced by mill variables, particle size, and material type.

the NSEC and EU of a three- roller mill can be predicted from the particle sizes of the milled product, the differential speed, the roll gap setting, the roll corrugation configuration, and the fast roll speed.
the energy required to reduce particle size of sorghum, corn, and wheat in a three- roller mill was directly proportional to the surface area of the product.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy consumption in a three-roll mill can be predicted from the particle size and surface area of the material.
the NSEC and EU are both dependent on the particle sizes of the materials and milled products.
the net specific energy and energy utilization of a three- roller mill for grinding cereal grains are functions of the particle size distribution of the material and the milled product.
